lesson.text: Quick memory: what is the climate like in a rainforest? (Hot and wet all year.) Many foods need a climate like that. Today: where our food comes from.
Almost all our food starts on a farm or in the sea. From farm to fork it is grown, harvested, sometimes made into something new (wheat into bread), carried to shops and sold.
Some foods need a hot, wet climate near the Equator: bananas, cocoa beans (for chocolate), coffee and pineapples. Most cocoa comes from West Africa, from countries like Ivory Coast and Ghana.
Other foods grow in milder places: wheat for bread, apples, potatoes and carrots. Rice grows best in warm, flooded fields, and most of the world's rice is grown in Asia.
Many foods travelled the world long ago: potatoes and tomatoes first came from South America, and oranges from Asia. Now they are grown in many countries.
Plants grow in their own season. In Britain strawberries ripen in summer and apples in autumn. Out of season, food comes from warmer countries or greenhouses.
Food miles are how far food travels from the farm to you. Bananas cross oceans by ship; carrots from a nearby farm may travel only a few kilometres.
Try it in the world: plant a farm with a patch for each crop, like wheat and pumpkins. Then build a market stall and put a sign by each food saying where it grows best.

exercises.prompt: Where does almost all our food start?
exercises.hint: Shops sell food, but where did the shop get it?
choices: on a farm or in the sea
exercises.explain: Almost all food starts on a farm or in the sea, and then travels to shops.

exercises.hint: It grows in hot, wet places near the Equator.
exercises.explain: Chocolate is made from cocoa beans.

exercises.prompt: Bananas grow best in hot, wet places.
exercises.hint: Think about the climate near the Equator.
exercises.explain: True: bananas need a hot, wet climate.

exercises.hint: Mimi the baker grinds a grain into flour.
exercises.explain: Bread is made from flour, usually ground from wheat.

exercises.prompt: Put the journey of bread in order.
exercises.hint: It starts in a field and ends in an oven.
items: the grain is ground into flour
exercises.explain: Grow the wheat, harvest it, grind it into flour, then bake the bread.

exercises.prompt: Where did potatoes first come from?
exercises.hint: Remember the foods that travelled the world long ago.
exercises.explain: Potatoes first came from South America, like tomatoes.

exercises.prompt: When are strawberries ready to pick in Britain?
exercises.hint: Find strawberries in the table, then read the season.
exercises.explain: Strawberries ripen in summer in Britain.

exercises.prompt: Most of the world's rice is grown in Asia.
exercises.explain: True: most rice is grown in Asia, in countries like China and India.

exercises.hint: The word miles tells you it is about distance.
choices: how far food travels from farm to plate
how fast a farmer can run
exercises.explain: Food miles are how far food travels from where it was grown to where it is eaten.

exercises.prompt: Why can you buy strawberries in winter in Britain?
exercises.hint: Is it their season in Britain in winter?
choices: they come from warmer places or greenhouses
exercises.explain: They are grown in warmer countries or in greenhouses, then carried here.

exercises.prompt: Cocoa grows well in cold places like Antarctica.
exercises.hint: Where does most cocoa come from?
exercises.explain: False: cocoa needs a hot, wet climate near the Equator.

exercises.prompt: Which food usually travels the most food miles to reach Britain?
exercises.hint: Which one cannot grow in Britain's climate?
exercises.explain: Bananas need a hot climate, so they cross oceans by ship to reach Britain.

exercises.prompt: On which continent are Ivory Coast and Ghana, where most cocoa grows?
exercises.hint: Find Ghana on a globe: it is just south of the Sahara desert.
exercises.explain: Ivory Coast and Ghana are in West Africa.

exercises.prompt: Sort these foods: which grow best in hot, wet places?
exercises.hint: Think of the climate near the Equator and the climate of Britain.
exercises.explain: Hot, wet places: bananas, cocoa, pineapples. Milder places: wheat, apples, carrots.

exercises.prompt: Match each food to where it grows or first came from.
exercises.hint: Remember the lesson cards about foods around the world.
exercises.explain: Most cocoa grows in West Africa, most rice in Asia, and potatoes first came from South America.

exercises.prompt: Sort the foods: from a plant, or from an animal?
exercises.hint: Did it grow in a field or on a tree, or did an animal give it?
exercises.explain: From plants: rice, chocolate (cocoa beans) and bread (wheat). From animals: milk, eggs and cheese (made from milk).

exercises.prompt: Order the foods from the most food miles to Britain to the fewest.
exercises.hint: The further the farm is from you, the more food miles.
exercises.explain: Bananas cross an ocean by ship: the most miles. Apples from France travel a few hundred kilometres. Carrots from a nearby farm travel only a few kilometres.

exercises.prompt: Match each food to the climate it grows best in.
exercises.hint: Cards 2 and 3: which foods need heat, which need flooded fields, and which grow in milder places?
exercises.explain: Bananas need a climate that is hot and wet all year. Wheat grows in milder places, like Britain. Rice grows best in warm, flooded fields.
